results.title: Marsch: Davies out for Canada's opener vs. Bosnia, Kone and Bombito available - Sportsnet.ca
highlights:
# Marsch: Davies out for Canada's opener vs. Bosnia, Kone and Bombito available - Sportsnet.ca
[...]
Faizal Khamisa is joined by a star-studded panel on the eve of the 2026 FIFA World Cup to discuss what success would look like for Team Canada, who should be the Golden Boot favourite, and much more.
[...]
Defender Moïse Bombito is available to play in Canada's World Cup opener, while captain Alphonso Davies has been ruled out.
[...]
But he was included on Canada's 26-man roster, and coach Jesse Marsch said he could play if needed against Bosnia-Herzegovina on Friday afternoon in Toronto.
[...]
"He'll be ready to contribute (Friday)," Marsch said. "He's not fully at 100 per cent, but he's reached his top speed. He's shown in training that every day he's getting stronger and better, and can focus more on football behaviours. I don't see any reason by a week from now that he's not ready to even be considered as a starter."
[...]
Marsch said the goal is "to get (Bombito) to 100 per cent."
[...]
Davies is the only player on the roster not available for Friday's game. He was expected to miss the match as he recovers from an injured hamstring, but was not officially ruled out until Thursday.
[...]
Marsch said Davies is progressing well.
[...]
"We did an MRI with him (Wednesday). It showed very positive signs that he's healing incredibly well, almost completely, so we're getting ready to ramp things up," Marsch said.
[...]
"He will not be available for (Friday), but I think that he's showing, like he always has, a real good ability to recover from muscle injuries. I think that having his private physio here has been very helpful, and the concentration on his body's needs every day, and so we're really hopeful that over the next days and weeks that we can accelerate things to give him a chance to contribute here soon."
[...]
Bombito was named to the initial 26-man World Cup roster, then logged 31 minutes in the squad's 2-0 friendly win over Uzbekistan on June 1. After leaving the field, he was spotted icing the injured leg.
[...]
Marsch said Bombito experienced "sensitivity" from the lingering injury, and that he would give him every chance to recover.
[...]
Marsch had until Thursday afternoon — 24 hours before Canada's World Cup opener against Bosnia — to replace any seriously ill or injured players.
[...]
He had already replaced midfielder Marcelo Flores, who will miss the tournament after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament on May 30.
[...]
Winger Jayden Nelson was named to the roster in Flores' absence.

results.title: Canada have 'advantage' to kick off home World Cup vs. Bosnia: ‘I don’t get nervous’ says Marsch - Waking The Red
highlights:
Canada’s long-awaited FIFA World Cup home debut finally arrives on Friday afternoon when the hosts face Bosnia and Herzegovina in Group B.
[...]
More than eight years after learning they would open the world’s largest tournament on home soil, Jesse Marsch’s side will step into the spotlight carrying the hopes of a nation eager to celebrate a historic moment — Canada’s first-ever men’s World Cup game played on Canadian soil and their first opportunity to earn a World Cup victory after previous winless appearances in 1986 and 2022.
[...]
“We know that tunnel, that pitch, the stadium, the fans, the Voyagers are going to be with us,” Stephen Eustáquio, who will captain Canada on Friday, told reporters including Canadian Soccer Daily, on Thursday evening. “Obviously, I hope right now that if everybody, the Canadians, are seeing this, that would they really help us get through this game and get a result at the same time. The fact that we’re going to play at the BMO is a very good thing for us. We’ve had a lot of good games at BMO. We know how it feels to step out of that tunnel and really push for the fans. So, I think that [on Friday] that’s an advantage. At the same time, we have to play the game.”
[...]
Canada enters the tournament with one of the most talented squads in its history, led by striker Jonathan David and a core of players competing in Europe’s top leagues. However, captain Alphonso Davies will miss the opener as he continues his recovery from injury, handing Marsch an early challenge against a disciplined Bosnian side. Toronto FC star Richie Laryea is expected to start at left-back. Toronto FC captain Jonathan Osorio played in both pre-World Cup tune-up friendlies this month and could come off the bench.
[...]
“To be honest, I don’t get that nervous,” Jesse Marsch said at Thursday evening’s press conference. “My job is to prepare the players to know what it’s going to require to go out on the pitch and do what they do. If I think back to different experiences, whether it’s when I was an assistant at the World Cup, when it was Champions League, Premier League, Bundesliga, or Copa America here, my focus and attention is always on the players and giving them the best opportunity to go out and be free, know their roles, and be themselves. We’ve accomplished that here over and over again.”

results.title: Injury reinforcements pledge to rise to occasion in Canada’s World Cup opener - The Globe and Mail
highlights:
For a team already bedeviled by injuries, Canada’s World Cup hopes ahead of Friday’s opener were hardly helped by the unexpected absence from training Wednesday of midfielder Ismaël Koné.
[...]
With team captain Alphonso Davies still working out by himself, which largely consisted of jogging slowly around the pitch at Toronto FC’s training complex north of the city, and fellow defender Moïse Bombito still limited in his involvement with the team, the news was far from ideal.
[...]
Canada’s midfield, which would likely consist of Koné and Stephen Eustáquio, should be relied upon to provide added protection for a makeshift defence, which will probably feature 20-year-old Luc de Fougerolles in Bombito’s absence, alongside veteran Derek Cornelius.
[...]
De Fougerolles is anything but intimidated though, and adds that the team’s friendly draw last Friday against Ireland in Montreal will have helped his team prepare for what’s in store. On top of that, he said his year-long loan from his regular club, Fulham, to Belgium’s Dender will also prepare him well.
[...]
… and then don’t give
[...]
While Bombito continues to work his way back from the broken leg he suffered last October, amid published reports that head coach Jesse Marsch will replace him on the 26-man roster in the next 24 hours, Cornelius – one of 13 holdovers from the last World Cup in Qatar – will be heavily relied on for his veteran poise at the back.
[...]
If he is alongside de Fougerolles against Bosnia, the 28-year-old Cornelius has full faith that the youngster won’t look out of place, despite the eyes of the planet being focused on Toronto Stadium come Friday afternoon.
[...]
“It’s his mentality, and for a game like this, it’s going to be a mental battle, especially on the physical side, and everyone knows that Luc is going to be up for that,” Cornelius said. “I think he’s gotten the trust of not only coaching staff but the group, and he’s earned that, and so everyone has full faith in him if he’s starting on Friday.”
[...]
Another Qatar veteran heading into his second World Cup is striker Cyle Larin. After finding himself on the sidelines and somewhat surplus to requirements at both Real Mallorca in Spain and during a loan to Feyenoord in the Netherlands, Larin found a new lease on his footballing life with a February move to Southampton in England’s second tier.
[...]
For a team that has found goals somewhat hard to come by in the last little while, getting the 31-year-old firing on all cylinders for country as well as club would be a boon for Canada’s chances. Despite netting 30 goals in his 90 appearances for the national team, Larin hasn’t scored for Canada since late 2024.
